Can Reservation Ever Be Removed From India? | Reservation System In India

Ever wondered why no political party in India whether BJP, Congress, or regional allies touches the current reservation system?

Together, Scheduled Castes (SC at 16.6%) and Scheduled Tribes (ST at 8.6%) form over 25% of the population, while Other Backward Classes (OBC) make up an estimated 40% to 50%. This creates a massive, consolidated 75% vote bank that no government can afford to displease.

We break down the historical timeline of affirmative action in India, starting from SC/ST reservation in 1950, its extension to education in 1951, the introduction of 27% OBC reservation post-Mandal Commission (1990â1992), to the 10% EWS quota in 2019, bringing total reservations to 59.5%. Discover why governments have repeatedly overruled Supreme Court verdicts, including the 50% cap limit and the application of the creamy layer rule to SC/ST categories.

 what it would legally and constitutionally take to eliminate reservation in India. From passing a Constitutional Amendment Bill under Article 368 requiring a two-thirds special majority in both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, to navigating the Supreme Court's Basic Structure Doctrine under Article 14 (Right to Equality and Social Justice). Is it legally possible, or is political consensus between ruling parties, opposition, and the judiciary an impossible hurdle? Watch the full video for a deep dive into Indian politics, current affairs, and constitutional laws.

3 years ago I created and filmed myself, building this Nike bedside cabinet. If you had told me building this one project would collectively be viewed by over 130 million people. I wouldâve said youâre crazy. Overnight my Instagram blew up. Thousands of DMâs asking to purchase the cabinet. I was truly overwhelmed. And not at all prepared. 

Obviously I was not in a position to build everyone a cabinet. So I didnât. Lots of people said I was crazy not to quit my job and pursue this opportunity. The truth is I didnât want to be known as the Nike box guy. Itâs just a box with someoneâs logo on it. I want to be known as the guy that makes one off, one of a kind pieces. 

Along with all the sneaker head viewers, I received lots of questions from woodworkers! This really excited me as Iâm passionate about sharing my craft. So I ended up creating a step-by-step build plan for the Nike cabinet. Which made a lot of people happy. Photos started flowing in of completed Nike cabinets. That was awesome to see. If youâre interested the build plans are linked in my bio. 

Currently still working full-time as a marine cabinet maker. For a company in New Zealand, which I really enjoy. But always in the back of my head Iâm thinking about whatâs my next Instagram reel going to be. Most of the work you see on my page, is me in my one car garage working with limited tools. 

Anyways thankyou for reading this far, stay tuned for the next creation!
Cheers Alex

Ever wondered how laser levels project a perfect line, or what music actually looks like? ð´â¡

This video demonstrates two creative, hands-on physics experiments involving lasers and mirrors. In the first project, a small mirror is attached to a spinning DC motor and mounted on a wooden block alongside a laser pointer and a bubble level. 

When turned on, the fast-spinning mirror scatters the laser dot into a straight, continuous red line across the room, illustrating the core working principle behind commercial laser levels.

In the second experiment, plastic wrap is stretched tightly over an empty bucket like a drumhead, with a small mirror glued to the center. When placed over a speaker playing music and hit with a laser pointer, the sound waves cause the plastic film and mirror to vibrate. 

This projects dynamic, dancing laser patterns onto the wall that react to every beat and note, allowing you to visually âseeâ sound without any digital effects.

This simple plastic clip uses old-school optical tricks to solve a massive headache for modern content creators.

Instead of buying a secondary overhead camera and dealing with complex broadcasting software, this attachment physically splits your smartphone's front-facing lens. By placing a small, 90-degree periscope mirror over exactly half of your camera, it redirects that portion of the sensor to look straight down at your desk.

The other half of the lens remains unobstructed to capture your face normally. The result is a perfect, real-time split screen showing both you and whatever you are writing, reading, or demonstrating on the table in front of you.

It is entirely hardware-based, meaning it works instantly with any standard camera app or video calling software. You get the benefit of a professional two-camera presentation studio without draining extra battery or requiring complicated app integrations.

It is a brilliantly low-tech solution to a high-tech problem.

Apple: Pair it with peanut butter or a handful of nuts for a more filling snack.

it can be superrr confusing and unclear how people are getting these roles, especially if youâre just starting out - so hereâs what actually helped me:

1.building real projects for your resume
building projects is so insanely easy now with ai tools and so many resources, but it can be hard to actually figure out what to build - so id recommend checking out the github repo linked to get inspo!

this is the first stage of the hiring process and the biggest drop off point. If youâre not getting any interviews itâs likely because of your resume. Make sure you maximize its potential with your existing experience

5.apply to roles the day they drop
this could easily be the difference between you getting a job and not, simply because you did or did not apply to roles when they came out. most companies review applications on a rolling basis - so you need to try to be one of the first ones in

Neither BJP nor TMC could ever win if India had elections like Japan.

â In Japan, the official election campaign period usually lasts just 12 days. Campaigning before that is illegal.

â Politicians cannot use religion during election speeches. Violating this can even lead to disqualification.

â Door-to-door campaigning is completely banned under election law.

â Candidates cannot put posters wherever they want. The government creates official poster boards with designated slots, and every candidate gets equal space.

â Instead of massive rallies, most candidates campaign through âsound trucksâ moving through neighborhoods announcing their names and short messages.

â Only officially registered campaign workers wearing government-approved armbands are legally allowed to campaign.

â Private TV election advertisements are heavily restricted. Candidates are instead given equal broadcast time. Paid targeted political advertisements on social media are also heavily restricted.

â Even giving small gifts, food, tea, or entertainment to voters can be treated as bribery.

â Campaign spending has strict legal limits and is closely monitored by authorities.

Japan showed the world that elections can be quiet, fair, and equal. That every vote can matter regardless of how much money stands behind it.

That is not just inspiring. That is possible.

Looking for a Business That Can Earn Even When Youâre Not Working?

Many people dream of building passive income, but the reality is that most passive income businesses require effort, time, and consistency before they start generating returns. The goal is not to make money overnight, but to build systems that can continue earning with less day-to-day involvement over time.

Some popular passive income models include ATM franchises, vending machines, self-service laundries, digital products, YouTube channels, blogs, and affiliate marketing. Each business has different investment requirements, risk levels, operational challenges, and earning potential.

While businesses like digital products, blogging, YouTube, and affiliate marketing may have lower startup costs, they often require significant time to build an audience. On the other hand, ATM franchises, vending machines, and laundries may require higher investment but can generate more predictable cash flow when located and managed properly.

There is no guaranteed passive income business. Success depends on market demand, execution, competition, consistency, customer acquisition, and long-term commitment.

label_values.value: This viral clip is everywhere right now, but most people are only getting half the story. The video claims India only spends $17 billion on education while the USA hits $1 trillion. That $17 billion figure only covers the Indian Central Governmentâs budget. In India, education is a "concurrent" subject, meaning state governments do most of the heavy lifting. When you combine the Centre and all States, Indiaâs total education spend is actually closer to $115â$120 billion. According to data from the Ministry of Education and PRS Legislative Research, India spends about 4.6% of its GDP on learning. The USA actually spends over $1.5 trillion annually on education when combining federal, state, and local funding. This massive investment accounts for roughly 5.4% of the US GDP as reported by the World Bank. China is also investing heavily with a total education budget reaching approximately $900 billion. Their spending consistently remains around 4.02% of Chinaâs total GDP. While the gap between these nations is significant, comparing a single Indian ministry to the total national spend of others is half information. To give you more depth, the "spend per student" is where the real difference lies. The US spends over $15,000 per student annually, while India's vast student population of 260 million means its per-student spend is much lower. In India, states like Himachal Pradesh and Kerala lead the way, spending nearly 15% of their total state budgets on education. India's literacy rate is projected to hit 78% in 2026, narrowing the gap with Chinaâs 97% and the US at 99%. Context is everything before you believe a viral chart. label_values.value: This 31-second reel explains how a modified South Korean coin exposed a costly flaw in Japan's vending machines. By drilling a hole through the coin, its size and weight closely matched a 500-yen coin, allowing the machine's sensors to accept it as genuine. Since the altered coin was worth only a fraction of the real currency, users could receive a drink along with legitimate Japanese change. As thousands of fake coins appeared across the country, vending machines began rejecting 500-yen coins altogether. To stop the scam, Japan introduced a redesigned 500-yen coin made from multiple metals with unique security features that counterfeit coins could not replicate.

Grid down. Network gone. Power out. Your smartphone isnât a brick if you cache data before a disaster strikes. By using your phoneâs internal sensors, it becomes a powerful, off-grid command center.

1. MESH MESSAGING: Bridgefy (Free)
Uses Bluetooth to connect to nearby devices (approx. 330 ft / 100m). Messages securely "hop" through intermediate users to daisy-chain a local network without cell towers.

Alternatives: Briar (Free, Android-only) adds peer-to-peer Wi-Fi mesh. Meshtastic (Hardware-dependent) links your phone via Bluetooth to low-cost LoRa radio nodes for true, miles-wide off-grid texting.

2. OFFLINE MAPS: Organic Maps (Free)
Your phone's internal GPS chip works without cell service. Download compressed vector maps of entire regions before grid failure to route vehicles, locate points of interest, and find addresses entirely offline.

Alternatives: Avenza Maps or CalTopo (Paid tiers available) are the gold standards for superimposing professional topographic maps and forestry charts over live offline GPS tracking.

3. CELESTIAL NAV: Stellarium (Free)
If GPS satellite arrays ever fail, manual direction-finding is your only option. Stellarium utilizes your phone's compass and gyroscope to transform your screen into an interactive astrolabe, enabling you to map constellations and locate the North Star even through thick smoke or cloud cover.

Alternatives: Spyglass (Paid) adds an advanced overlay featuring an AR compass, sextant, and tactical waypoint tracker.

4. MEDICAL: Red Cross First Aid (Free)
Caches critical trauma diagrams and step-by-step animations directly to your device. Get instant instructions for tourniquet application, severe bleeding, and CPR when emergency infrastructure is completely overwhelmed.

5. KNOWLEDGE: Army Survival Manual (Free)
This app packages field-proven military manuals (like FM 21-76) into an offline text database covering primitive shelters, water purification, and emergency signaling.

â ï¸ THE GOLDEN RULE: Digital tools are never a guarantee. Batteries die and software glitches. Use these apps to augment your capabilities, but always carry physical paper maps, a magnetic compass, and hard-copy manuals in your pack.

Most people reach for the lid instinctively â and leave it on without thinking. The lid itself is never the problem. The moment you put it on is. âªï¸ Comment below â which dish always disappoints you?#steam101 #cookingscience #foodscience #lidtiming #flayvah

This is the most common kitchen myth â that a lid makes the pan hotter. It doesnât. With the lid off, steam escapes and evaporative cooling slows the temperature rise, but surfaces can go above 100Â°C. With the lid on, less evaporation means faster heating â but temperature stays capped near 100Â°C because trapped steam limits how hot the environment inside the pan can get. Two completely different heat environments. Same flame.
#cookingscience #steamscience #lidmyth #kitchenfacts #flayvah

Look at those two pans of mushrooms. Same mushrooms. Same heat. Same oil. The only difference is the lid â and the result looks like two completely different ingredients were cooked. Lid on: steam condenses back into the food. It stays wet. It softens. It never browns. Lid off: moisture escapes. The surface dries. Structure sets. Browning begins. This is why your vegetables go limp â not because of the recipe.
#mushroomrecipe #cookingscience #moisturecontrol #texturematters #flayvah

Rice starch gelatinizes between 65 and 75Â°C. If thereâs excess surface water trapped with the rice when this happens, the starch leaches out of the grain and bonds neighboring grains together. Thatâs your sticky, clumpy rice â and it happens because the lid trapped condensation back onto the rice at exactly the wrong moment. Lid off during the final stage lets that surface moisture escape instead of seeping back in. Light, separate grains are a steam decision, not luck.
#ricerecipe #perfectrice #stickyricefix #cookingscience #flayvah

Most people think garlic is justâ¦ garlic.

But the way you cut it completely changes its flavor.

Hereâs why:

ð§ Sliced garlic is the mildest. It damages fewer cells, so less allicin is produced. Perfect when you want a subtle, aromatic garlic flavor that wonât overpower a dish.

ðª Minced garlic creates a stronger, sharper taste because more cells are broken, allowing more sulfur compounds to form.

ð¥ Crushed garlic delivers the boldest flavor. Crushing releases the most allicin, giving garlic its intense aroma and pungencyâideal for marinades, dressings, and recipes where you really want garlic to shine.

ð¥ Roasted whole garlic is a completely different experience. Slow cooking deactivates the enzymes responsible for garlicâs sharp bite, allowing its natural sugars to caramelize into a sweet, buttery, almost nutty flavor.

One simple trick many chefs use? Let chopped or crushed garlic sit for 10â15 minutes before cooking. This gives the enzyme alliinase enough time to convert alliin into allicin, maximizing both flavor and many of garlicâs beneficial sulfur compounds before heat begins to deactivate the reaction.

Cooking isnât just about ingredientsâitâs about understanding the science behind them. Small techniques like these can completely transform the taste of your meals without adding extra calories, salt, or sugar.

The Loosdrecht Lakes in the Netherlands are home to hundreds of houses built on incredibly narrow strips of land, creating one of the country's most unique neighborhoods.

Today, boats often replace cars, and the area has become a popular destination for boating, kayaking, and waterfront living.

NEFT vs RTGS vs IMPS vs UPI: Which Payment Method Should You Use for Fast, Secure and Hassle-Free Money Transfers?

India offers multiple digital payment systems, each designed for different types of transactions. UPI is widely used for everyday payments, IMPS enables instant bank transfers, NEFT is suitable for general fund transfers without an RBI-prescribed minimum amount, while RTGS is primarily meant for high-value transactions with a minimum transfer amount of â¹2 lakh.

Although all four payment methods are available 24Ã7, they differ in transfer speed, transaction limits and ideal use cases. UPI and IMPS are generally preferred for instant retail payments, NEFT is commonly used for routine bank transfers, and RTGS is typically chosen for large-value transfers that require real-time settlement.

Transaction limits, charges and features may vary depending on your bank, account type and RBI guidelines. Before initiating high-value transfers, always verify the latest limits and applicable policies with your bank.

ð¦ DAY 28/30 â FIFO, LIFO, FEFO, LEFO, HIFO & LOFO Explained
Managing inventory isn't just about storing productsâit's about deciding what goes out first.
Different inventory methods help businesses reduce waste, control costs, and improve operational efficiency.
Here's a quick overview:
ð¹ FIFO (First In, First Out) â Oldest inventory is issued first.
ð¥ Best for food, beverages, and retail.
ð¹ LIFO (Last In, First Out) â Newest inventory is issued first.
ð¦ Used in specific inventory/accounting scenarios.
ð¹ FEFO (First Expiry, First Out) â Products with the earliest expiry are issued first.
ð Essential for pharmaceuticals and food industries.
ð¹ LEFO (Last Expiry, First Out) â Products with the latest expiry are issued first.
ð¨ Used in selected inventory situations.
ð¹ HIFO (Highest In, First Out) â Highest-cost inventory is issued first.
ð° Sometimes used for inventory valuation.
ð¹ LOFO (Lowest In, First Out) â Lowest-cost inventory is issued first.
ð Used in certain pricing strategies.
Choosing the right inventory method can improve inventory accuracy, reduce losses, and support better supply chain decisions.

Macros Per Serving (5 Total)

518 Calories | 49g Protein | 55g Carbs | 12g Fat

Ingredients (5 Servings)

Orange Pepper Chicken
- 1100g Raw Boneless Skinless Chicken Thighs, trim any excess fat
- 1 Tsp Salt
- 2.5 Tsp Black Pepper
- 2.5 Tsp Garlic powder
- 30g Honey
- 25g Sriracha
- 1 Large Orange Juiced + Orange Zest. I like to add bits of the pulp in the marinade for extra caramelized texture

â¢ Marinate chicken for 30 mins or overnight for maximum depth of flavor
â¢ Spread evenly on a lined sheet pan, squeeze extra orange juice and zest. This will caramelize while cooking and create a sticky glaze.

Crunchy Cucumber Salad
- 250g Mini Cucumbers, thinly sliced
- 100g Red Onion, thinly sliced
- 120g Carrots, grated
- 100g Red Bell Pepper, chopped
- 50g Green Onion/Scallion
- 25g Sesame Seeds
- 15g Honey
- 20-25g Rice Vinegar

ð¡Meal Prep Tip
Keep the salad in separate meal prep containers and combine right before eating to maintain crunch. The vinegar base helps preserve the texture for 2-3 days

Garlic Butter Herb Rice
- 220g Uncooked Basmati Rice 
- 20g Light Butter
- 30g Garlic, finely chopped
- 1.5 Tbsp Fresh Parsley, chopped

The prostate gland contains the highest zinc concentration of any organ in the human body â and zinc deficiency is directly linked to impaired testosterone synthesis, reduced sperm motility, and increased prostate cancer risk through immunological and hormonal pathways ð¬

Zinc is required at the final enzymatic step of testosterone biosynthesis, where the enzyme 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase performs the conversion to active testosterone. Without adequate zinc, this step stalls regardless of other hormonal health factors. This is why zinc deficiency consistently produces low testosterone symptoms â fatigue, low libido, reduced strength â even in men whose LH and FSH levels appear normal.

Sperm cells have the highest metabolic demand per cell of any cell type in the body, and zinc is critical for DNA packaging inside sperm cells, acrosome reaction function, and the antioxidant protection that prevents sperm DNA fragmentation. Low zinc produces measurably impaired sperm motility and higher DNA damage rates ðª

Research published in the Journal of Human Reproductive Sciences found that zinc supplementation in zinc-deficient men for 12 weeks produced significant improvements in total sperm count, sperm motility, testosterone levels, and fertilization rates compared to placebo.

One mineral. Three critical male health systems.

Most men are mildly deficient and have no idea.

One of the most common questions I hear is:

"Should I stop eating rice and only eat roti?"

The answer is: No.

Neither rice nor roti is automatically better for diabetes. What matters most is how much you eat and what you eat with it.

To help keep your blood sugar more stable:

â¢ Watch your portion size.
â¢ Pair rice or roti with a good source of protein such as chicken, fish, eggs, lentils, or beans.
â¢ Fill half your plate with non-starchy vegetables like cucumber, spinach, or cauliflower.
â¢ Avoid eating large portions of rice or roti on their own.

A balanced meal has a much bigger impact on your blood sugar than choosing one carbohydrate over another.

There's no need to fear your favorite foods. Learning how to build a balanced plate is the key.

ð¥ Eggs â Hair Growth
Eggs are rich in high-quality protein and biotin. Since hair is made primarily of keratin (a protein), getting enough protein helps support normal hair growth.

ð¥¬ Spinach â Hair Fall Support
Spinach provides iron and folate, which help carry oxygen to hair follicles. If hair fall is related to low iron levels, improving iron intake may help.*

ð¥ Almonds â Hair Strength
Almonds contain Vitamin E, an antioxidant that supports healthy hair and scalp, helping reduce damage and breakage.

ð Salmon â Healthy Scalp
Salmon is rich in Omega-3 fatty acids, which support a healthy scalp. A healthy scalp creates a better environment for healthy hair.

ð Orange â Collagen Support
Oranges are high in Vitamin C, which helps the body produce collagen and also improves iron absorptionâboth important for healthy hair.

ð« Lentils â Healthy Hair Roots

Prospective Fellows: Help mission-driven organizations put AI to work for good

Claude Corps is a fully funded, 12-month paid fellowship that places early-career talent inside mission-driven nonprofits. Fellow applications are open to anyone over the age of 18 with less than two years of full-time work experience who is authorized to work in the United States. There is no education requirement. We are looking for fast learners who have everyday comfort with AI tools, work well with others, can clearly communicate their ideas, and have a demonstrated drive for societal impact.

Three organizations run Claude Corps together. Anthropic funds the program, leads its overall strategy, and provides Claude expertise. CodePathâa national nonprofit focused on technical educationârecruits, trains, and employs fellows as the employer of record. Social Finance administers the programâs philanthropic capital and leads measurement and evaluation.

The benefits of transformative AI systems could come at the cost of significant disruption. The companies building this technology have a responsibility to make sure the benefits are fully realized and widely shared, and to invest directly in the workers absorbing the change. As such, anthropic is committing an initial $150m to this program.

Applications and timeline:
Fellowship applications are open today, and will close on July 17th for the first cohort of 100, which begins in October 2026. Applications are open on a rolling basis for the next two cohorts, which begin in January 2027 and August 2027. Anyone over 18 with under two years of full-time work experience is welcome to apply, regardless of educational background. The only requirements are that youâre authorized to work in the US, are comfortable working with Claude, and are willing to relocate if necessary. (Relocation support is available as needed.)

Host organization applications are also open today for all cohort start dates. For more information about criteria for hosting and whatâs involved, see the Claude Corps website.

You do not need to invent a product from scratch to build a massive business.

The secret is white labeling: importing a ready-made product from China, putting your logo on it, and selling it as your own.

Here is the exact step-by-step checklist to white-label your first product:

1ï¸â£ Find your supplier: Go to Alibaba, search your product, and filter for verified and trade-assured suppliers only to protect your money. (Use 1688 if you read Chinese).

2ï¸â£ Send the first message: Open the chat and ask, "I want to white-label this under my own brand. What's your MOQ, unit price, and can you send a sample?"

3ï¸â£ Check importability: Before paying anyone, search your product's ITC-HS code on the DGFT portal to ensure it is "Free" to import, not Restricted or Prohibited. Remember, some "Free" items still need approvals like FSSAI (food), CDSCO (cosmetics), or BIS (electronics).

4ï¸â£ Get your IEC: Apply for an Import Export Code from the DGFT. It is your mandatory passport for importing, takes about a day, and costs almost nothing.

5ï¸â£ Order a sample first: Never skip this step. Put your branding on it and test the quality before ever committing to a bulk order.

6ï¸â£ Lock and ship: Finalize your packaging, confirm the bulk order, and sort out your logistics and customs duty.

There is more to navigate, including duty math, exact IEC steps, and customs agents. I packed this entire process, plus a ready-to-send supplier message template, into one full checklist.

Samsung might be one of the most diversified companies in the world.

Most people know Samsung for smartphones and televisions, but the company operates across industries that seem completely unrelated.

Samsung manufactures advanced semiconductors used by companies around the world, produces OLED displays for devices including smartphones, builds electric vehicle batteries, operates one of the world's largest shipbuilding businesses, and develops major industrial projects such as oil refineries and petrochemical plants.

Beyond manufacturing, Samsung also operates businesses in advertising, biotechnology, construction, and entertainment, including South Korea's largest theme park.

The reason Samsung looks so unusual is because it was built as a conglomerate, a business model designed to operate across multiple industries instead of depending on a single market.

The strategy creates advantages through scale, technology, and internal capabilities. But it also requires managing complexity across very different businesses.

Samsung's story shows that some companies don't win by dominating one category. They build ecosystems that allow them to compete in many.

VIPâs Dilip Piramal openly admitted that âa change of management had become a necessityâ as the company was losing share and his daughters didnât want to run it.

Most promoter families have 70â90% of their wealth locked inside one illiquid company. On paper theyâre rich. In reality, theyâre over-exposed.

Meanwhile, valuations have run up. The India consumption story is hot, and global capital is chasing it.

So what do families do?
They do what any good investor would do: de-risk.

Sell a big stake to PE.

Pay off debt.

Set up a family office.

Diversify into real estate, global funds, PE/VC, philanthropy.

Thatâs why the number of Indian family offices jumped from about 45 in 2018 to around 300 in 2024.

Plus, a lot of these companies simply outgrew the promoterâs skill set.

Running a 50-crore regional brand is one thing.
Running a 1,000-crore national or global company in a world of eâcommerce, GST, AI, and global competitors is something else entirely.

Who is most affected by global shipping loopholes?ð¢
The global shipping industry operates on a complex legal structure that remains largely invisible to the public. Mongolia, a completely landlocked nation situated between China and Russia and located over 700 kilometers away from any ocean, currently operates an open ship registry established in 2003 that hosts approximately 3,000 registered vessels, with around 500 of them actively operational. This phenomenon is part of a global framework known as Flags of Convenience, under which an estimated 72 to 73 percent of the world's merchant fleet is registered in smaller jurisdictions like Panama, Liberia, and the Marshall Islands rather than the home nations of the actual shipowners.

You pay Airtel. Airtel pays someone. That someone laid cables under the ocean. Hereâs the full chain.â¨
The internet runs on three levels.â¨
At the top Tier 1 companies. AT&T, NTT, Tata Communications. These companies own the physical cables on land and under the ocean. They donât pay anyone for internet access because they are the internetâs backbone. The actual physical infrastructure the entire worldâs internet runs on.â¨
Below them Tier 2. Airtel, Jio, BSNL. These companies buy bandwidth from Tier 1 per Gbps per month. More bandwidth needed, more they pay. They take that bandwidth and spread it across India through cell towers and fiber lines.

Below Tier 2 Tier 3. Local cable operators, small ISPs. They buy from Tier 2 and distribute locally. And at the bottom you. Paying your local ISP or Airtel directly.
Tier 1 â Tier 2 â Tier 3 â You.â¨
Now the real question what is Tier 1âs physical infrastructure? 95% of Indiaâs internet comes through undersea fiber optic cables. Not satellite. Not wireless. Literally cables laid on the ocean floor from India to America, Europe, and Southeast Asia. These cables land at Mumbai and Chennai coastlines at cable landing stations, connect to Indiaâs land fiber network, reach Airtel and Jio towers, and finally reach your phone.

These cables are as thick as a garden hose 69mm. Inside multiple fiber optic strands, each thinner than a human hair. But one cable carries 200 terabits per second. Mumbai to London 11,000 kilometers undersea signal reaches in 60 milliseconds.â¨
And one fact nobody knows sharks bite these cables. Electromagnetic fields attract them. Modern undersea cables are built with shark-proof coating.
400+ undersea cables worldwide. Total length 13 lakh kilometers. 30 times around the Earth.
Thatâs the internet. Physically.

In this clip from âSuryamani Bhagat: Saving Forests in Jharkhandâ by Global Greengrants Fund in 2015, Suryamani Bhagat speaks about how colonial forest laws, particularly the Forest Act of 1927, alienated Adivasi and forest-dwelling communities from forests they had protected and depended on for generations. What had once been a shared relationship with land was turned into a system of control, where indigenous communities were denied rights over their own resources and livelihoods.

She then reflects on the long struggles and resistance movements that led to the passing of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 - a landmark law that recognised the âhistorical injusticeâ faced by tribal and forest communities in India. The Act was not simply about land ownership. It acknowledged the role of indigenous communities as protectors of forests, ecosystems, and traditional knowledge systems that have sustained both people and biodiversity for centuries.

Through her work with the Jharkhand Jangal Bachao Andolan, Suryamani Bhagat has continued to organise communities around forest rights, conservation, seed preservation, and sustainable living practices rooted in indigenous knowledge. At a time when conversations around climate change and sustainable development dominate public discourse, her words remind us that environmental protection cannot be separated from justice, community rights, and the lived knowledge of people who have coexisted with forests long before sustainability became a global framework.

Your phoneâs GPS has limits most people never notice.

Many GPS devices include what are known as COCOM limits, restrictions designed to prevent civilian navigation systems from being used in high-speed military applications. The rule generally disables or restricts GPS functionality when a device is operating above certain altitude and velocity thresholds. 

Contrary to popular posts online, this is not a hidden âkill switchâ inside every smartphone specifically designed to stop missile building. It is a long-standing safeguard built into many commercial GPS systems. Companies like Apple and other manufacturers use GPS technology that must comply with regulations aimed at limiting military misuse. 

The result is a little-known example of how national security concerns can shape the technology millions of people use every day.

Did you know your GPS could be restricted under certain extreme conditions?

Viral Battery Apps Are Scaring E-Rickshaw Drivers!â ï¸What's Really Happening?

Apps like BAT-BMS and LOSSIGY have recently gone viral after social media posts claimed they could connect to nearby Bluetooth-enabled e-rickshaw batteries and even interfere with battery settings. These apps are legitimate battery management (BMS) tools designed to monitor and configure compatible lithium battery systems, but viral videos have raised concerns that unsecured Bluetooth connections could potentially be misused if a battery's BMS lacks proper security. 

The trend has sparked fear among e-rickshaw (Tirri) owners, who worry that strangers could tamper with their vehicles or disrupt their livelihood. While there is no confirmed evidence of widespread real-world attacks using these apps, the controversy has highlighted the importance of securing Bluetooth-enabled BMS devices with passwords, updated firmware, and manufacturer-recommended settings. Experts also note that BMS security depends on the battery manufacturer, not the app alone.

label_values.value:
Playboi Carti and Don Toliver represent two distinct, yet equally impactful, forces in contemporary hip-hop. Carti, a pioneer of the "rage" microgenre, is known for his eccentric vocal style, often employing a "baby voice" and focusing on mood and persona over traditional lyricism. His music is characterized as atmospheric and avant-garde, blending influences from punk and metal into his hip-hop roots, as seen in his album "Whole Lotta Red" (2020). His latest album, "Music," released in March 2025, further cements his unpredictable and experimental approach, featuring a diverse range of sounds from R&B-infused tracks to aggressive punk records and electric trap beats. Carti's influence extends beyond his own releases, as his Opium label has fostered a new wave of artists who embrace a similar aggressive, distorted sound and punk aesthetic.

Don Toliver, on the other hand, brings a unique blend of hip-hop, R&B, and trap, captivating listeners with his melodic delivery and versatility. His sound often features a similar use of auto-tune to Travis Scott, creating an airy and spacy vibe. Toliver's career has seen a meteoric rise since his breakout single "No Idea" and his signing to Travis Scott's Cactus Jack Records in 2018. His discography includes successful albums like "Heaven or Hell" (2020), "Life of a Don" (2021), "Love Sick" (2023), "Hardstone Psycho" (2024), and his most recent, "Octane," which debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 in January 2026. Toliver is currently on his "Nitrous World Tour," showcasing the explosive demand for his music.

The claim that creators can make thousands of dollars daily via fake streams highlights a rapidly growing ecosystem of automated digital fraud, click farms, and AI manipulation that heavily distorts online engagement. Your feeling that the "internet is fake" closely mirrors the Dead Internet Theory, an idea gaining traction as autonomous bots and AI avatars outnumber or replace genuine human interactions. 

While individual viral claims of making exactly $10,000 every single day may be exaggerated to sell courses or software, massive operations utilizing these exact tactics are pulling in staggering amounts of real-world revenue.

How the "Fake Internet" Makes Money

Massive Phone View Farms: Click farms use specialized cloud software to sync thousands of physical devices simultaneously. For example, a court case reported by the South China Morning Post revealed a operator who used 4,600 mobile phones to artificially inflate livestream counts, earning over $415,000 in less than four months.

AI Clones and 24/7 E-commerce: Creators are building hyper-realistic digital avatars of themselves or fictional influencers to stream endlessly. On platforms like Baidu, automated AI clones have successfully generated millions in e-commerce sales over short windows without a human ever stepping in front of a camera. 

Donation and Subscription Scams: Fictional AI-generated personalities and automated "thirst trap" streams are deployed on social platforms to push viewers toward closed memberships, generating thousands in monthly recurring revenue from fans who believe they are interacting with a real person. 

Algorithmic Manipulation: Specialized tech rings construct arrays of hundreds of smartphones mounted to walls or ceilings, streaming targeted content non-stop. This tricks platform recommendation algorithms into pushing low-effort content to real users, maximizing programmatic ad revenue.

If you get an interview and make it through a couple rounds, the last thing most companies will have you do for a video editing role is make a trial edit. This is a chance to show what you can do, so make sure to keep working on getting better in the offseason.

That was just the beginning. Sanofi dives deep into natureâs strangest tools from venoms to antibodies to bacteria and engineers them into precise medicines. They use massive robot labs to test millions of molecules against disease targets then run years of clinical trials with real patients to make sure they work safely. The result? Over one hundred different medicines reaching more than one hundred million people every year. Think about it the iron in your blood or the way your immune system fights invaders these same principles get copied and improved to create treatments for diabetes cancer and rare diseases. What started as pure curiosity about how a toxin works became pills that let grandparents see their grandkids grow up. The coolest part is the next big cure might be sitting inside something we currently fear like a spider bite or a virus. Science like this is constantly turning the impossible into the everyday. Old money style is a fashion aesthetic that embodies understated elegance and timelessness. Rooted in the traditions of the American upper class, particularly those with long-established wealth, old money style is less about following trends and more about maintaining a classic, refined appearance.

At the heart of this style is an emphasis on quality over quantity. The garments are often simple, with clean lines and a neutral color palette, favoring materials like cashmere, wool, and cotton. Pieces such as tailored blazers, crisp Oxford shirts, loafers, and pearls are staples of the old money wardrobe. These items are chosen not for their flashiness but for their durability and versatility, often passed down through generations.

Accessories in the old money style are minimal yet meaningful. Watches, often understated luxury brands like Rolex or Patek Philippe, are worn for their craftsmanship rather than as status symbols. Jewelry is subtle, with a preference for heirloom pieces that carry sentimental value rather than large, ostentatious designs.

This style extends beyond clothing to encompass a way of life, emphasizing discretion, education, and cultural pursuits. Old money style is less about displaying wealth and more about a quiet confidence that comes from a deep-seated sense of heritage and belonging. Itâs an approach to fashion that values longevity, with each piece chosen for its ability to stand the test of time, both in style and construction.

In essence, old money style is an embodiment of grace, restraint, and a deep respect for tradition, where the focus is on a legacy of elegance rather than the fleeting nature of trends.

A viral video is gaining attention online after explaining the difference between flat interest rates and reducing balance interest rates on loans.

According to the creator, many borrowers focus only on the advertised interest percentage without understanding how the interest is actually calculated. The video explains that under a flat interest structure, interest is charged on the original loan amount throughout the loan tenure, while under a reducing balance structure, interest is calculated on the remaining principal amount as repayments are made.

The clip has sparked discussions among vehicle buyers and loan applicants, with many viewers saying they were unaware of the difference before watching the video. Others emphasized the importance of comparing the total repayment amount rather than looking only at the interest rate.

As the video continues to trend, it is encouraging more people to learn about loan terms, EMI calculations, and financial literacy before making borrowing decisions.

Wheezy crafted a dreamy, atmospheric instrumental filled with floating melodies, deep bass, and crisp drums that perfectly matched Gunnaâs effortless delivery. The beat gives the song its smooth late-night feel, allowing Gunna to ride the production almost effortlessly from beginning to end.

A big reason the track connected with listeners is how naturally Gunna and Wheezy complement each other musically. Their chemistry has produced some of Gunnaâs most recognizable songs, and âWho You Foolinâ is another example of that formula working perfectly.

The Most Expensive Shot Iâve Ever Taken ð­ð­ð­

While filming these flamingos with my DJI Mavic 4 Pro, the drone accidentally hit an electric line and crashed into the saltwater lagoon.

First, no birds were harmed or disturbed. I maintained a safe distance and used the zoom lens camera to capture these moments responsibly. Please donât attempt flights like this without proper experience and professional guidance.

DJIâs tracking system helped me locate the crash area, but I was disappointed that the drone completely powered off after the impact. I ended up walking nearly 5 km through the lagoon to find it, only to discover it was completely dead from saltwater damage.

The biggest worry wasnât the drone it was the footage. Everything was recorded on the droneâs 512GB internal storage. Even DJI couldnât help recover the data, but thankfully a skilled technician managed to save it.

This incident cost me nearly â¹4,00,000 and taught me a huge lesson: always keep a backup and donât rely only on internal storage.

The drone is gone, but the footage survived.

And honestly, for moments like these, I still feel it was worth it.

ðï¸ Planning to buy a new bike? Donât focus only on the ex-showroom price.

Hidden charges added at the dealership can increase your final bill by â¹20,000ââ¹30,000 or more.

Swipe through before making your payment. â¡ï¸

ð Check logistics and handling charges carefully.

If the bike is already available at the showroom, ask why an additional logistics fee is being charged.

Request a detailed cost breakup and understand exactly what youâre paying for.

ð§¾ Never ignore âincidental charges.â

These are often dealer-added fees and may not be mandatory government charges.

Always ask what services are included and whether you can opt out.

ð ï¸ Before paying separately for Roadside Assistance (RSA), check your insurance policy.

Many insurance plans already include services like towing, battery support, and breakdown assistance.

Donât pay twice for the same coverage.

ð Look closely at service and Pre-Delivery Inspection (PDI) charges.

A new bike is usually inspected and prepared for delivery as part of the dealerâs responsibility.

Ask why these charges are listed separately on your quotation.

âï¸ Verify the accessories list before making payment.

Standard items such as mirrors, saree guards, toolkits, and basic fittings are often included by the manufacturer.

Ensure youâre not being charged again for accessories that come with the bike.

ð Always ask for a complete on-road quotation.

Review every charge line by line instead of focusing only on the final amount.

If you donât understand a fee, ask questions before making the payment.

ð° A bike priced at â¹1 lakh can cost thousands more because of hidden charges.

Stay informed, review every detail, and pay only for what you actually need.

Land mafias in India have evolved. It is no longer just about gundas and threats. Today it is a coordinated network of retired revenue officials, cooperative society secretaries and property lawyers working together systematically. They change records, revive inactive societies, file fake cases and register sale deeds on land that does not even exist. By the time the original owner realises what happened, the land has already changed hands multiple times. This is a crime of paperwork and that makes it far more dangerous than anything a gunda could do.

Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) is a technique that controls the average power of an electrical signal by rapidly switching a digital voltage on and off. It "fakes" an analog output by varying how long the signal stays "HIGH" (on) versus "LOW" (off) within a repeating cycle.
....A PWM signal is fundamentally defined by two main factors:Duty Cycle: The percentage of time the signal is "ON" relative to the total period of one cycle. A 50% duty cycle means the signal is on for half the period.Frequency: How many times per second the cycle repeats (measured in Hertz). Inertial loads require frequencies high enough to prevent visible flickering or jerking.By adjusting the duty cycle, you can easily control the average voltage delivered to a device (\(V_{avg}\)):\(V_{avg}=\text{Duty\ Cycle}\times V_{source}\)Core ApplicationsBecause PWM provides an incredibly energy-efficient way to control power, it is ubiquitous in modern electronics:Motor Control: Adjusts the speed of DC motors by controlling the average current.LED Dimming: Rapidly flashes LEDs faster than the human eye can perceive, tricking the brain into seeing lower brightness without overheating the components.Microcontrollers: Allows digital boards (like Arduino or ESP32) to generate variable analog results without a built-in Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC).AdvantagesHigh Efficiency: Instead of "burning" excess voltage off as heat (as a traditional linear resistor would), PWM acts as a rapid switch, dissipating almost zero power during its off-cycles.Cost-Effective: Generating a PWM signal requires very little silicon, making it a highly economical feature on most microprocessors.

The Psychology of Pink Hair

Pink hair occupies a specific cultural position that has shifted dramatically over the past two decades. What once read as rebellion, the punk dye job, the signal of deliberate outsider status, has moved steadily toward the mainstream without fully losing its original charge. It still means something, just not the same thing it used to.

The choice to dye your hair pink is rarely purely aesthetic. It is a statement about visibility, about willingness to be seen and categorized, about opting out of the professional and social camouflage that natural hair colors provide. According to a 2021 survey by StyleSeat, pink was the most requested unconventional hair color in the United States, with searches for âpink hairâ peaking on Google Trends during the pandemic years, when people had more freedom to experiment away from office environments.

The interpretation depends heavily on context. On a teenager it reads as exploration, on a woman in her forties it reads as confidence, on a corporate employee it reads as a negotiation between identity and institution. The same color carries different weight depending on who is wearing it, which says more about how we read appearance as biography than it does about the color itself.

Prostate enlargement affects 1 in 2 Indian men after 50.

But hereâs what most people donât realize:

The prostate is one of the few organs that never stops growing after age 25. 
By your 60s, it can go from the size of a walnut to a lemon. 
The condition is called Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia and it directly impacts how you urinate, sleep, and live.

Modern sedentary lifestyles, chronic stress, belly fat, and Indiaâs high-carb low-protein diet are accelerating prostate growth faster than previous generations. 

Simple changes in your 20s and 30s can significantly slow this down. 
Swipe through to find out! 

Prostate growth after 25 is completely normal biology. Every man goes through it. 
The question is when it becomes troublesome. If you notice any changes in urination or discomfort, consult a urologist. 
Early awareness makes all the difference.

The sophisticated research carefully notes that this rapid-fire processing system does not mean that a beautiful personality or facial charm are secondary or unimportant in long-term human bonding. Anna (2019) â blends stylish espionage, brutal action, and nonstop twists into a sleek assassin thriller. Directed by Luc Besson, the film follows Anna Poliatova, played by Sasha Luss, a young Russian woman whose modeling career hides a far more dangerous reality as a highly trained KGB assassin.

What starts as a straightforward spy story quickly becomes layered with shifting timelines, double-crosses, and hidden motives. Much like Bessonâs earlier films such as La Femme Nikita and LÃ©on: The Professional, the movie mixes elegance and violence, presenting Anna as both vulnerable and extremely lethal.

One of the filmâs standout moments is a long restaurant fight sequence that was praised for its choreography and fast, fluid camera work. Sasha Luss, who had mostly been known as a fashion model before the film, surprised many viewers with the physicality and confidence she brought to the role. The cast also includes Helen Mirren, Cillian Murphy, and Luke Evans.

Beneath the stylish action and espionage, Anna is really about control and survival. Nearly every character is manipulating someone else, and the film constantly asks whether true freedom is even possible in a world built on secrets and power.

No GPS. No signal. 400 meters underwater. Yet a submarine knows exactly where it is.
Hereâs the engineering behind it.â¨
GPS runs on radio waves. Seawater absorbs them almost instantly signal strength halves every meter. At 400 meters depth, GPS is completely dead.â¨
So submarines use INS Inertial Navigation System.â¨
Inside INS are two core sensors. Accelerometers measure movement across all three axes. Integrate acceleration once you get velocity. Integrate again you get position change. Ring Laser Gyroscopes handle direction two laser beams fired in opposite directions inside a closed loop. When the submarine rotates, one beam travels a slightly longer path, creating a phase difference. That phase difference directly gives rotation rate precise to 0.001 degrees per hour.â¨
Every fraction of a second position and direction updated. No external reference needed.â¨
But thereâs a problem. Accelerometers have microscopic errors sensor noise, bias. Integrated over time, these errors compound. Even the best military INS drifts nearly 1 nautical mile every 24 hours.â¨
The fix Terrain Contour Matching.â¨
The ocean floor has mountains, trenches, plains a unique topographic fingerprint. This map is pre-stored in the submarineâs computer. Sonar pulses fire downward, return time is measured, ocean floor depth is calculated. That terrain profile is matched against the stored map and exact position is locked. No signal. Just the shape of the ocean floor.â¨
Submarines also use Doppler Velocity Log, acoustic positioning, and brief GPS fixes at periscope depth but INS and TERCOM are the core.
Weeks underwater. Zero external signal. Kilometer-level accuracy.
Pure physics.

YouTuber Yosh has spent years using reinforcement learning for his Trackmania AI experiments. 

His latest agent is now driving the game at a level almost no human can reach.

After roughly 2,000 hours of in-game training, the AI has finished the A06 track in 27.55 seconds. That puts it 0.05 seconds behind the world record of 27.50 set by Link, a time the community has spent years chasing.

The AI starts with no knowledge of the game and learns through repeated runs, shaped by a reward tied to lap time. Every input, every drift, every brake is something it figured out on its own.

Despite running over 2,000 simulated hours of training â compressed into roughly 50 real-world hours â the AI peaked at 27.55 seconds and never managed to close that final 0.05-second gap. The result surprised even its creator, showing that raw training time is not always enough to overcome a skilled humanâs perfectly optimized technique.

When people say âsearch save Sudan on Google Maps,â theyâre usually reacting to viral posts claiming youâll see shocking satellite imageryâbut the reality is more complicated. Most of what appears are random map pins, mislabeled locations, or low-resolution satellite images that can easily be misinterpreted. Sudan is a vast country with deserts, villages, and scattered activity, and from space, things like cattle, water points, or shadows can look dramatic or disturbing without context.
Online discussions (especially on forums) show that many of these âdiscoveriesâ are either misunderstood visuals or exaggerated claims, not verified evidence. Some pins may even have been removed or hidden over time, adding to the mystery. The important thing is that while Sudan is facing real humanitarian issues, Google Maps is not a reliable source to confirm such claimsâitâs easy for the eye to be fooled by satellite imagery without proper context.

Kolkata was not always a city the world forgot. It was the city the world came to. The economic capital of British India. Home to the countryâs biggest port, its most powerful industries, and 27% of Indiaâs entire industrial output. If you wanted money, power, or opportunity in pre-independence India â you came to Kolkata.

Then 1947 happened. The Partition didnât just redraw borders. It ripped the supply chain of an entire city apart overnight. 75% of jute fields went to East Pakistan. All 106 mills stayed behind in India with nothing to process. The refugee crisis broke the infrastructure. The port started silting. Investors got nervous and then they got out. Dunlop. IISCO. Jessop. One by one, the giants fell.

Today West Bengal holds just 5.6% of Indiaâs GDP. Its per capita income sits 20% below the national average. States that didnât even exist a decade ago have already overtaken it. Kolkata still has the talent, the history, and the hunger. The only question left is whether anyone is willing to bet on it again.

A family in Kolkata is making Indiaâs first indigenous underwater robots.

Banergy â started by the Banerjee family â is building ROVs and USVs for underwater inspection, river mapping, and hydrographic surveys.

They have been testing the equipment at Prinsep Ghat on the Hooghly River.

Current prototypes are a simple cylindrical ROV with dual thrusters and an unmanned surface vehicle with a catamaran structure. All built in India.

The company partners with Blue Robotics â an authorized distributor â for global parts coupled with Indian engineering.

The objective is simple: lower Indiaâs reliance on foreign-made marine technology.

Underwater survey and inspection activities in India are dominated by imported technology.

Banergy is here to change this.

Rakhi Banerjee (Managing Director), Swarnab Banerjee (Operations), and Rishav Banerjee (Engineering), leading the team, say Banergy was âborn from Indian rivers.â

Itâs a start-up that actually builds something, tests it in real-world conditions, and focuses on addressing a very real problem.

India's rivers, ports, and coastline are in need of inspection, mapping, and surveillance.

Kolkata Calcutta, Bengal elections, West Bengal, British Empire, Bengal partition, Swadeshi Movement, Khudiram Bose this is the city that scared the British Empire.

In 1911 the British did something unthinkable.

They took the capital of India away from Calcutta.

Officially it was called an administrative decision.

But Bengal knew better.

Because after the 1905 Bengal partition, Calcutta stopped behaving like a colony.

Swadeshi movement exploded. 
British goods were burned. 
Revolutionaries emerged. 
Bombings began. 
Khudiram Bose became a martyr at just 18.

And suddenly the British Empire â which ruled half the world â no longer felt safe ruling India from Bengal.

That is what made Calcutta different.

This was not just a city.

It was the political nerve centre of anti-British resistance.

And maybe that is why this story still matters emotionally during Bengal elections even today.

Because cities do not just lose power economically.

Sometimes power is taken away politically.

So the real question is:

Did the British shift the capital for administration

or because Calcutta had become too politically dangerous to control?

Some cities grow with time.
Kolkata helped shape time itself.

From Asiaâs first tram system to one of the worldâs oldest cricket stadiums, from historic courtrooms to bridges that became symbols of an entire city â these places are not just landmarks. They are chapters of Indiaâs modern history.

The streets of Kolkata carry institutions, engineering, architecture, transport systems, and cultural spaces that influenced generations far beyond Bengal itself.

What makes these places special is not only age or recognition.
It is the fact that they still live with the city every single day.

Trams still move.
The bridge still carries millions.
The library still preserves knowledge.
Eden still roars.

History here was never locked inside museums.
It became part of everyday life.

Save this post if you love learning about the legacy of Kolkata and share it with someone who should know how deeply this city shaped India.

Some have homes in Europe, luxury properties in their home countries, and private estates in places like England, Spain, Italy, and the Middle East.

Priyanka Gandhi - Strongly criticised govt on accountability

In a recent speech in Parliament, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra strongly raised the issue of government accountability, questioning the moral responsibility of top leadership in times of national concern. She argued that accountability is the cornerstone of democracy and must apply equally to those holding the highest offices.

Her remarks were particularly directed toward the roles of the Amit Shah and Rajnath Singh. Without making purely personal allegations, she emphasized that when serious lapses or failures occur-whether related to internal security or national defence-the ministers in charge must take responsibility. She suggested that accountability should not remain a symbolic concept but must translate into concrete action, including resignation when necessary.

Priyanka Gandhi criticized what she described as a pattern where the government avoids direct responsibility and shifts focus through political narratives. She argued that in a healthy democracy, resignations are not signs of weakness but of integrity and respect for public trust. According to her, such steps strengthen institutions rather than undermine them.

She also highlighted the need for transparency and open discussion in Parliament, stating that elected representatives have a duty to question the government without fear. Her speech framed accountability as a duty owed to citizens, especially when national security and governance failures are under scrutiny.

Overall, her address was a sharp call for ethical governance, insisting that those in power must be held answerable not just politically, but morally, to the people of India.

Corruption does not always begin with massive scams or thousands of crores.

According to the CMS India Corruption Study 2018, departments linked to daily public services reported some of the highest levels of unofficial payments and influence.

From:
â¢ Driving licences
â¢ FIR registration
â¢ Land records
â¢ Utility connections
â¢ Hospital services

millions of Indians deal with these systems every year.

The dangerous part is not just the bribe itself.
It is when corruption slowly starts feeling normal in everyday life.

Interestingly, banking services reported the lowest corruption levels in this list, showing how digitisation and tracking systems can reduce human interference.

Because when shortcuts become a culture, trust in the entire system slowly breaks down.

India has improved in many areas.
But the bigger question still remains:

Can transparency and digital systems actually reduce everyday corruption at scale?

Most people think âautomaticâ is just automatic.
But AMT, CVT, IVT, DCT, DSG, Torque Converter and iMT are completely different gearboxes.

AMT is basically a manual gearbox where actuators change gears for you. Cheapest automatic, usually great for mileage, but also the jerkiest.

CVT has no fixed gears. It uses pulleys to keep the engine in its efficient RPM range. Super smooth in traffic, but that rubber-band effect when you floor it is why enthusiasts hate it.

IVT is Hyundai/Kiaâs version/name for their CVT-style transmission.

DCT uses two clutches. One for odd gears, one for even gears. Thatâs why shifts are super quick. DSG is Volkswagen Groupâs name for its dual-clutch gearbox. Great for performance, but not always the happiest in crawling traffic.

Torque Converter is the old-school automatic that uses fluid coupling. For most Indian buyers, this is probably the best all-rounder: smooth, reliable, comfortable, and highway-friendly.

iMT is clutchless manual. You shift gears yourself, but thereâs no clutch pedal.

Best for comfort + reliability? Torque Converter.
Best for mileage + city smoothness? CVT / IVT.
Best for performance? DCT / DSG.
Cheapest automatic? AMT.
Manual feel without clutch pain? iMT.

Because automatic is not one thing anymore.

Murshidabad, Kolkata, Calcutta, Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore, Bengal, West Bengal, Mamata Banerjee, Plassey, Robert Clive, Siraj ud Daulah, Mir Jafar this is the story of the Indian city that was once richer than London and then disappeared from power.

Before Kolkata became Indiaâs great colonial city, Murshidabad was one of the richest places in Asia.

A financial capital. 
A silk and muslin hub. 
A city where British, French, Dutch and other European powers competed for influence.

Robert Clive himself compared Murshidabadâs wealth and population to London.

Then came 1757.

Battle of Plassey.

Siraj ud Daulah lost. 
Mir Jafar switched sides. 
And the British slowly shifted trade, administration and political power away from Murshidabad and into Calcutta.

That is the moment Bengalâs power map changed forever.

Calcutta rose.

Murshidabad faded.

And today, while Kolkata still dominates Bengalâs identity and politics, Murshidabad remains one of West Bengalâs poorer districts with large-scale migration for work.

That is what makes this story feel so haunting.

Because cities do not collapse overnight.

Power leaves them slowly.

Investment leaves them slowly.

Attention leaves them slowly.

And eventually the country forgets what they once were.

So the real question is:

Can places like Murshidabad ever rise again

or once power leaves a city, does it almost never return?

Until 1784, Bombay was still seven fractured islands â separated by tidal creeks that swallowed land twice a day.

That physical unification changed everything.

Trade accelerated.
Roads became reliable.
Cotton moved faster.
Railways became possible.
Industry followed.

Tamil Nadu, Haryana, Punjab, Tamil language, Punjabi language, Bansi Lal, ML Khattar Tamil speech, Pongal celebration, North vs South this is one of Indiaâs strangest political stories.

For nearly 40 years, Tamil was Haryanaâs second official language.

Not Punjabi. 
Not Urdu. 
Tamil.

Even though Haryana had almost no Tamil-speaking population.

No major Tamil schools. 
No large Tamil-speaking community. 
No real public use of Tamil.

And yet it stayed inside Haryana government records for decades.

Why?

Because after Haryana separated from Punjab in 1966, the new state needed a second official language.

But politically, Haryanaâs leadership did not want Punjabi.

So Bansi Lal reportedly chose Tamil because it carried no local political baggage.

That is what makes this story fascinating.

One Indian state officially adopted another stateâs language

not because people spoke it

but because politics made it useful.

Then in 2010, Haryana finally replaced Tamil with Punjabi.

Which is why ML Khattar speaking fluent Tamil during a Pongal celebration shocked the internet years later.

Indiaâs language politics is stranger than fiction.

At the edge of Hyderabad, Aurva Illam by IKI Builds (@iki.builds) unfolds as a constructed terrain - where architecture is shaped as much by climate as by intent.

No AC. No marble. No glass. Just quarry debris poured into thermal walls, rammed earth revealing the site's own geology, terracotta vaults trapping insulating air, and a cantilevered granite staircase that barely touches the wall. 

Aurva Illam in Kadthal, Hyderabad, by IKI Builds is what regenerative architecture looks like when it stops making excuses and starts making decisions.

In resisting spectacle, Aurva Illam provokes a timely questionâcan restraint and material honesty redefine our idea of luxury?

label_values.value:
Apple made an ad. Then made a video about making the ad. And the second one went more viral than the first.
This is not a coincidence â it's the smartest marketing shift happening right now. Coinbase did the same thing with their "Your Way Out" campaign. The ad looked like a video game â but there was no CGI and no AI involved. Real actors wore printed suits and custom low-polygon face masks of their own faces, performing NPC choreography on handmade pixelated sets. It was insane to watch. And then Coinbase dropped the BTS of all of it everywhere. Here's why this works â AI can now generate any visual in seconds, so people have completely stopped being impressed by what something looks like. What they actually value now is effort, craft, and human process. So brands are no longer just selling the product. They're selling the story of how hard they worked to make it. BTS has gone from bonus content to the core of the entire campaign. And this trend is only getting bigger â in the next one to two years, every major brand will be doing this.
The ad about the ad is the new ad. Are you already using this for your own content?

label_values.value:
What started as a solar energy project in India eventually became a case on Adani in American courtrooms.

This story has everything: Power contracts, alleged bribery, global fundraising, WhatsApp chats, international law, and billion-dollar negotiations.

The most interesting part is that the alleged bribery itself did not happen in the US.

The reason American regulators got involved was because Adani Green had raised money from US investors through dollar bonds while allegedly claiming full compliance with anti-bribery laws.

And that brings us to one of the most important concepts in global finance:
Once you raise money from international investors, local problems can quickly become global legal issues.

The entire case also shows how deeply connected todayâs corporate world has become.

A power contract in India.
Bonds sold in America.
Global investors funding the project.
US anti-corruption laws entering the picture.
And eventually, settlements negotiated across continents.

Whether one agrees with the allegations or not, this case will probably be studied for years in corporate finance, governance, and international business law classrooms.

Because sometimes the biggest business stories are not about profits.

They are about how power, capital, regulation, and geopolitics collide behind the scenes.

Green Zone Land buying rules in Maharashtra have CHANGED for 2026. If you are looking at farmland, farmhouse plots, or second homes, read this before you sign any deal. ðð

A lot of investors look at a cheap piece of land in Karjat, Alibaug, or along the Samruddhi Mahamarg and think itâs a golden opportunity. But in Maharashtra, a low price tag often comes with heavy legal restrictions.

Before you park your hard-earned money into Green Zone property, you must understand the rules:

â The Eligibility Trap: You cannot legally purchase agricultural land in Maharashtra unless you are a registered agriculturist. Finding "workarounds" can lead to massive legal battles and title disputes.
â The Construction Myth: Buying Green Zone land does NOT mean you can automatically build your dream villa. Without an NA (Non-Agricultural) conversion, zoning approval, and a valid Commencement Certificate, your construction is completely illegal.
â Hidden Costs: The land price is just the starting point. Stamp duty, registration, legal vetting, fencing, zoning approvals, and architect compliance can easily add lakhs to your actual budget.

Ever wondered how IPL broadcasts show â106m SIXâ within seconds of the ball landing?â¨
No tape. No laser. No manual measurement.â¨
Hereâs what actually happens:â¨
10 high-speed cameras mounted on the stadium roof track the ball continuously from before the bowler even starts his run-up.â¨
Every few milliseconds, the system identifies the ballâs pixel cluster from at least 2 cameras simultaneously. Since both cameras are physically calibrated at known positions in the stadium, two projected lines from two different points can only intersect at one location in 3D space. Thatâs the ballâs exact X, Y, Z coordinate. This is called triangulation.â¨
This repeats hundreds of times while the ball is in the air  building a complete 3D flight arc in real time.â¨
When the ball descends, the system tracks its Z coordinate (height) dropping frame by frame. The moment Z hits zero thatâs the landing point locked.â¨
Distance is then calculated from bat contact point to first landing point. Not from the crease. Not from the boundary rope. Bat to first bounce.â¨
That number on your screen? Hundreds of 3D coordinates â captured, triangulated, and calculated in the time it takes you to blink.
This is Hawk-Eye.

The Mil Mi-6 (NATO name: "Hook") was a 44,000 kg Soviet behemoth that fundamentally changed helicopter design by proving that "heavy-lift" wasn't just for fixed-wing aircraft. When it first flew in 1957, it was twice as large as any other helicopter on Earth and held the title of the world's largest rotorcraft for nearly 15 years. The technical "wow" point is its removable stub wings. Because the massive 35-meter main rotor couldn't provide enough lift for high-speed flight without risking aerodynamic stall (retreating blade stall), engineers added two 15-meter wings that generated up to 20% of the aircraftâs total lift during cruise. This allowed the Mi-6 to reach a record-breaking top speed of 300 km/h (186 mph), a feat previously thought impossible for a machine of its size.

Structurally, the Mi-6 was the world's first large-scale production helicopter to utilize **turboshaft engines**, moving away from the heavy, vibrating piston engines of the era. Its two Soloviev D-25V engines produced a combined 11,000 shaft horsepower, which was managed by the R-7 gearboxâa component so massive it actually weighed more than the two engines combined. This raw power allowed the Mi-6 to transport 12,000 kg (26,000 lbs) of internal cargo, ranging from armored vehicles to 90 paratroopers, which it loaded through massive rear clamshell doors. From fighting fires to supporting the Chernobyl liquidators, the Mi-6 proved that with enough power and a set of auxiliary wings, even a "flying bus" could dominate the skies.

Quantitative finance uses principles from Game Theory to model situations where multiple market participants make strategic decisions that affect one anotherâs outcomes. Financial markets are competitive environments where traders, hedge funds, market makers, and institutions constantly react to each otherâs behavior. Game theory helps quants analyze these interactions and design strategies that remain profitable even when other participants respond.

One key application is in market microstructure and execution strategies. When a large institution wants to buy or sell a significant position, it must consider how other traders might react if they detect the order. Game-theoretic models help determine optimal order execution methods that minimize price impact and prevent other traders from exploiting the trade.

Game theory is also used in auction design and market making. Exchanges operate as competitive environments where liquidity providers adjust their bidâask spreads while anticipating the behavior of other market makers. Quants use strategic models to decide how aggressively to quote prices without taking excessive risk.

Another area is adversarial trading environments, such as high-frequency trading. Firms must anticipate how competing algorithms will react to price movements, order book changes, or arbitrage opportunities. Game-theoretic reasoning helps model these interactions and design strategies that remain robust when competitors attempt similar trades.

Before writing a single note for Black Panther, Ludwig GÃ¶ransson knew the score had to be rooted in real culture, not imitation. After reading the script, he traveled to Senegal to study West African music firsthand, working directly with local musicians and learning how rhythm functions as language, history, and identity.

Those experiences shaped the foundation of the soundtrack. GÃ¶ransson recorded traditional instruments such as talking drums and the Fula flute, building character themes from their natural textures.
TâChallaâs identity emerged through layered drum patterns, while Killmongerâs theme used sharp, aggressive flute tones to reflect his anger, pain, and inner conflict.

Back in the studio, GÃ¶ransson blended these recordings with orchestral scoring and modern production. The result felt both ancient and futuristic - grounding Wakanda in real musical tradition while giving the film epic cinematic scale. The score redefined what a superhero soundtrack could be and earned GÃ¶ransson the Academy Award for Best Original Score.

Inside the device you are reading this on right now, a critical component you might never have heard of is beavering away. âInstruction set architecturesâ (ISA) are the interface between the hardware and software in every computing device. They are essentially sets of rules that translate code into instructions that microchips can understand and execute. Without them, no device - whether a smartphone or a supercomputer - would be able to function. 

Most ISAs are proprietary and used under licence. This costs money - and it restricts the ability of users to design custom chips based on their specific requirements. 

RISC-V is an open-source ISA that is free to use, designed explicitly to be customised, and which is already found in billions of devices and computers around the world. Hereâs how it works.

âDRAAKâ â So rich, he had to buy two.. ð¤¯
.
.
There's a level of wealth where owning a superyacht isn't the flex anymore. The real flex is owning a second smaller yacht whose only job is to follow the first one around. That's called a support vessel. And that's exactly what âDRAAKâ is.

âDRAAKâ is a 91.5-meter Oceanco megayacht, built in 2014 in the Netherlands. Her sole purpose is to accompany âLEVIATHANâ, the 111-meter mother ship of Gabe Newell, the billionaire co-founder of Valve and the man behind Steam, the world's biggest PC gaming platform. A support vessel carries everything you don't want cluttering your main yacht: tenders, water toys, extra crew, helicopters, equipment. While âLEVIATHANâ stays clean and open, âDRAAKâ handles the rest.

But âDRAAKâ 's story doesn't start with Gabe Newell.. Before all of this, she had two completely different lives. She was originally built as âEquanimityâ in 2014 for Malaysian financier Jho Low, using an estimated $250 million of funds embezzled from a sovereign wealth fund. She was seized by authorities in Bali in February 2018, after a tourist spotted her and tipped off the FBI. Then sold at auction in April 2019 for just $126 million (roughly half her build cost) she became âTranquilityâ (you can see naming pattern right there), entered the charter market, and was famously chartered by Kylie Jenner for her birthday. Then in 2023, Gabe Newell bought her, renamed her âDRAAKâ (Dutch for "dragon") and sent her back to Oceanco for a full re-build, and relaunched her in February 2026 as his personal support yacht.

Born in Houston, Texas, Scottâs early years were defined by a restless creative energy that eventually led him to drop out of college to pursue music in Los Angeles and New York. This period of struggle forged the "La Flame" personaâa relentless artist who refused to accept anything less than stardom. His early mentorship under Kanye West provided the platform he needed to introduce his signature sound: a dark, atmospheric blend of trap and psychedelic rap.

The sonic landscape of a Travis Scott project is characterized by heavy distortion, lush synthesizers, and intricate layers of auto-tuned vocals. His debut studio album, *Rodeo*, established him as a pioneer of "rockstar rap," but it was 2018âs *Astroworld* that cemented his legacy. Named after a defunct Houston theme park, the album served as a sonic amusement park, blending high-energy rages with melodic introspection. His music is often described as "curated chaos," where every beat switch and guest feature is placed with the precision of a master architect.

Beyond the audio, Scottâs brand is a powerhouse of collaborative innovation. Through his "Cactus Jack" imprint, he has partnered with brands like Nike to create some of the most sought-after sneakers in history. His ability to turn a performance into a cultural event was best exemplified by his record-breaking virtual concert in *Fortnite*, which redefined the possibilities of live digital entertainment. Despite significant controversies, Scott remains a central figure in the zeitgeist, continuing to push the boundaries of psychedelic sound and visual storytelling. RuView GitHub Repository is an open source project that uses normal WiFi signals and AI to detect movement, breathing, and body position through walls.

Instead of cameras, it studies how wireless signals change when people move inside a room.

The system works with low cost hardware like ESP32 chips and regular WiFi routers, making the technology far more accessible than expensive military style equipment.

Developers believe it could be useful for healthcare monitoring, smart homes, and emergency rescue situations.
